parties:
Nurul Amin Chowdhury ----------- Petitioner. 
Vs.
Chairman, Second Labour Court, Dhaka and ors ------------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Amin Chowdhury, J. : This Rule Nisi was issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh against the judgment dated 29.5.85 passed by the Chairman. 2nd Labour Court, Dhaka dismissing the Complaint Case No. 72 of 1983 filed by the present petitioner before us. 

 2. The short facts leading to the issuance of the Rule Nisi is, that the petitioner joined as Supervisor of Kohinoor Battery Manufactures Ltd. in the year 1969 and on 11.9.82 during an altercation with one Delwar Hossain he was assaulted and beaten up at the instigation of one Borhanuddin who was a foreman of the aforesaid Company. The petitioner lodged a petition of complaint whereupon both himself and Delwar Hossain were asked to show cause on 19.9.82 on the allegation of creating riotous indiscipline in the Mill area. The petitioner submitted his representation on 29.3.82 denying the allegation but the management found the explanation not satisfactory and set up an Inquiry Committee. The Inquiry Committee asked the petitioner to appear before them on 16.10.82. The petitioner appearing before the Committee raised objection as to the constitution of the Inquiry Committee for including one Mr. Abdur Rashid as member secretary of the said Committee and prayed for reconstitution of the said Inquiry Committee by changing Mr. Abdur Rashid but his prayer was turned down. His further case is that he also made representation to the Chairman, Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation on repeated occasions for replacing Mr. Abdur Rashid from the Inquiry Committee but without any result and thereafter the respondents without holding any inquiry dismissed the petitioner from service by their Order dated 8.8.83. The petitioner then put in his grievance petition and on being unsuccessful filed the Complaint Case No. 72 of 1983 in the Second Labour Court, Dhaka against his dismissal. The Labour Court after examining witnesses and on perusal of the record of the inquiry proceeding by its judgment dated 29.5.85 dismissed the case. The petitioner then moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Mr. Azizul Huq, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that tile Labour Court committed illegality in holding that the petitioner was given an opportunity to place his defence before the Inquiry Committee and that the said Committee illegally held the inquiry and recommended for taking appropriate action against the petitioner. He further submits that the Labour Court illegally found that the inquiry was held with due and proper notice to the petitioner and that the petitioner had all the opportunities to place his grievances before the Inquiry Committee. He further submits that the Labour Court ought to have held that notice dated 20.10.82 by which the petitioner was directed to appear before the Inquiry Committee was not actually served upon the petitioner and the inquiry was conducted at the back of the petitioner and that the witnesses were also examined in the absence of the petitioner which has materially prejudiced the petitioner's case and resulted in miscarriage of justice. 

 4. Mr. Sk. Abul Hossain. learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the contesting respondents, submits that the petitioner was duly notified of the date for appearing before the inquiry committee on 24.10.82 but he deliberately avoided to appear before that committee. He further submits that the Inquiry Committee after examining witnesses recommended for taking disciplinary action and the Labour Court also after examining witnesses and on perusal of the inquiry report and other materials produced before it rightly dismissed the petition of complaint and thereby it has not committed any illegality. 

 5. It is well-settled that Labour Court is not a Court of appeal but it can interfere only when the Inquiry Officer or the Inquiry Committee, as the case may be, acts unfairly and against the principles of natural justice. 

 6. Its function is to see whether the delinquent is lawfully punished. It is also well-settled that the Inquiry Officer or the Inquiry Committee is only required to follow the procedure laid down in sub-section (1) of section 18 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act. The Labour Court can only interfere with the finding of the Inquiry Officer or Inquiry Committee if it is found that the inquiry was held unfairly, with bad faith without complying with the principles of natural justice and without following the procedure laid down in the aforesaid section 18 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act. Here in the present case before us the allegation of the petitioner is that the inquiry was conducted behind his back without notifying the petitioner and the Labour Court failed to appreciate that aspect of the matter. It has been argued that the Labour Court illegally dismissed the complaint though as a matter of fact there is absolutely no evidence before it to hold that the inquiry was held in presence of the petitioner and he had the opportunity to place his case before the Inquiry Committee and examined witnesses. 

 7. Before the Labour Court the petitioner got himself examined as P.W. 1 and his definite case is that notice dated 20.10.82 directing him to appear before that Enquiry Committee on 24.10.82 was not served upon him and the inquiry was held behind his back. During cross-examination also he denied the suggestion that he received notice dated 20.10.82. The respondent examined one Reazuddin Ahmed as D.W. 1. In his examination-in-chief he stated that the notice dated 20.10.82 was served upon the petitioner. The notice was produced before the Labour Court and marked as Ext. D. We have gone throe, this Ext. D and it is found that nowhere it has been mentioned that the same was served upon the petitioner. D.W. 1 frankly admitted that the administration section of the Mills told them that this notice was served and as such they held the inquiry. Excepting this nothing was produced before the Labour Court to show that notice dated 20.10.82 was served upon the petitioner. D.W. 1 also admitted that there was no postal receipt showing despatch of Ext. D by post nor that there was any other proof of its being despatched. Before the Labour Court none from the administration section of the Mill was examined to prove that actually notice dated 20.10.82 was served upon the petitioner. Admittedly Inquiry Committee proceeded with the inquiry and examined witnesses on 24.10.82 and 26.10.82. D.W. 1 admitted that the petitioner was not intimated about the fixing of date on 26.10.82 and he further admitted that witnesses were examined on these two dates. 

 8. From the perusal of the papers filed it is found that the respondents produced the papers of the Inquiry Committee which was marked Ext. E. by the Labour Court and it is found that the petitioner appeared before the Committee on 16.10.82 and answered certain questions and thereafter on the ground of his illness he left the Committee. The Inquiry Committee on that date has not fixed any other date but subsequently by Order dated 20.10.82 they fixed 24.10.82 and from the materials before us it is found that the same was not notified to the petitioner and the inquiry was conducted at his back. It is also found that the Inquiry Committee submitted it report on 15.3.83 and thereafter the petitioner was dismissed by the Management by Order dated 8. 8. 83 and which Order the petitioner received on 14.8.83. The petitioner then put in his grievance petition on 21.8.83. Thereafter the grievance petition was disposed of on 10.9.83 and that order has been marked as Ext. 1 before the Labour Court. The petitioner being aggrieved then filed the petition of complaint before the Labour Court. 

 9. The Labour Court though examined the petitioner as P.W. 1 and one Reazuddin as D.W. 1 and though it had materials before it the Labour Court failed to appreciate that the petitioner has not received notice dated 20.10.82 by which the inquiry committee fixed 24.10.82 for hearing the matter. The Labour Court has not directed its decision to wards that. That is the crux of the whole problem. If an inquiry is held at the back of a delinquent or without notifying the delinquent it cannot be found that-the inquiry was conducted in accordance with the provisions of section 18 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act. The evidence adduced from the side of the respondent clearly proved that no notice was served upon the petitioner or that the petitioner has not received the notice dated 20.10.82 by which the Inquiry Committee fixed 24.10.82 as the date of hearing. Thus after consideration of the materials on record we are of the view that the inquiry was conducted behind the back of the petitioner and this inquiry is not an inquiry in the eye of law and not in accordance with the provisions of section 18 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act. The Labour Court failed to appreciate this aspect of the matter. The Labour Court, therefore, illegally came to the finding that the allegation that the petitioner was not given the proper opportunity for his defence is not at all tenable. We have carefully gone through the evidence of D.W. 1 and it is found that the Labour Court failed to notice the evidence of this witness at all and has not entered into the matter to decide whether the notice was actually served upon the petitioner or not. Having given our anxious consideration to the materials on record we are of the view that the inquiry conducted was unfair and not in accordance with law. 

 11. Thus after consideration of the materials on record, we are of the view that the Labour Court illegally dismissed the petition of complaint and it failed to exercise the jurisdiction vested in it and as such it requires interference by this Court. 

 12. The Rule, is accordingly made absolute but without any order as to costs. We hereby declare that the proceeding before the Inquiry Committee and the Labour Court has done and taken Without any lawful authority and IS of no legal effect. 

 Let the Labour Court's records be sent down at once.
